summary: A man who wronged a woman without marrying her may still marry her relatives, but not the relatives of his wife. Rabbi Yehudah adds a case that he forbids.

chunks.en: One may marry the relative of a woman who was forced or tricked.
chunks.explain: These women were wronged by a man who did not marry them.
chunks.st: One may marry a relative, e.g., the sister or the mother, of the woman he raped and of the woman he seduced.

chunks.en: But one who forces or tricks a relative of his wife
chunks.st: However, one who rapes and one who seduces a relative of the woman who is married to him

chunks.he: חַיָּב. נוֹשֵׂא אָדָם אֲנוּסַת אָבִיו וּמְפֻתַּת אָבִיו,
chunks.en: is guilty. A man may marry a woman his father forced or tricked,
chunks.st: is liable to receive capital punishment or karet for engaging in prohibited sexual intercourse, depending on the particular family relationship. A man may marry a woman raped by his father, or a woman seduced by his father, or

chunks.en: or one his son forced or tricked.
chunks.st: a woman raped by his son, or a woman seduced by his son.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah forbids a woman forced
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda prohibits marriage

chunks.en: or tricked by his father.
chunks.st: in the case of a woman raped by his father or a woman seduced by his father.

summary: When a woman becomes a Jew together with her sons, the sons do not count as brothers for yibum or chalitzah. The same is true for a freed maidservant and her sons.

chunks.en: A convert woman whose sons became Jews with her
chunks.st: With regard to a female convert whose sons converted with her,

chunks.en: they do not do chalitzah or yibum,
chunks.explain: Becoming a Jew is like being born again, so they are not counted as brothers.
chunks.st: they do not perform ḥalitza for each other’s wives, and they do not perform levirate marriage with them, as their conversions are considered rebirth, and they are considered unrelated. This is so

chunks.en: even if the first son was conceived
chunks.st: even if the conception of the first son

chunks.en: before she became a Jew and born after,
chunks.st: was not in the sanctity of Israel, i.e., the mother had not yet converted when she conceived of him, but his birth was in the sanctity of Israel, as his mother had converted by the time she gave birth to him,

chunks.en: and the second was conceived and born after.
chunks.st: whereas the second son was both conceived and born in sanctity. The first son is considered a convert, who is unrelated to his brother.

chunks.en: And the same is true for a maidservant whose sons were freed with her.
chunks.st: And this halakha similarly applies to a maidservant whose sons were freed with her, as they too are not considered relatives.

summary: Five mothers' babies got mixed up, so nobody knows which boy belongs to which mother. When they grew up, married and died, each widow needs chalitzah from four brothers and then may do yibum with the fifth.

chunks.en: Five women whose babies got mixed up,
chunks.st: With regard to five women whose offspring were mixed, i.e., their lineage became indeterminate, and they had other sons as well who were not mixed,

chunks.en: and the mixed-up boys grew up, married women, and died.
chunks.st: and the mixed sons matured and married women and subsequently died,

chunks.en: Four brothers do chalitzah with one widow,
chunks.explain: Each from a different mother, so one of them must be her real brother-in-law.
chunks.st: then four sons who were not mixed, each one from a different mother, must perform ḥalitza with one of the widows, as she might be the sister-in-law of any of them.

chunks.en: and one does yibum with her.
chunks.st: And one son of the mother whose sons did not perform ḥalitza may perform levirate marriage with her instead of ḥalitza; even if she is not his sister-in-law, once she has received ḥalitza from the others she may marry any man.

chunks.en: He and three others do chalitzah with another widow,
chunks.st: Subsequently, he and three of the four other sons must perform ḥalitza with one of the remaining widows,

chunks.en: and one does yibum.
chunks.st: and the other one may perform levirate marriage.

chunks.en: So there are four chalitzos and one yibum
chunks.st: When this process has been completed for all the widows, four ḥalitzot and a levirate marriage are found altogether

chunks.en: for each and every one.
chunks.st: for each and every widow.

summary: A grandmother's baby was mixed up with her daughter-in-law's baby. So one is the other's uncle, but no one knows which. The mishnah teaches who may do yibum and who only chalitzah.

chunks.en: A woman whose baby got mixed up with her daughter-in-law's baby
chunks.st: With regard to a woman whose offspring was mixed with the offspring of her daughter-in-law, and their lineage was consequently indeterminate,

chunks.en: the mixed-up boys grew up,
chunks.st: and the mixed sons matured and

chunks.en: married women,
chunks.st: married women, and subsequently

chunks.he: וּמֵתוּ, בְּנֵי הַכַּלָּה חוֹלְצִין וְלֹא מְיַבְּמִין,
chunks.en: and died. The daughter-in-law's sons do chalitzah, but not yibum,
chunks.st: they died, the certain sons of the daughter-in-law perform ḥalitza with the wives, but not levirate marriage,

chunks.en: because she may be his brother's wife
chunks.st: as with regard to each wife it is uncertain whether she is his brother’s wife, and therefore his yevama, and

chunks.en: or his uncle's wife.
chunks.st: uncertain whether she is his father’s brother’s wife, who is forbidden to him.

chunks.en: And the grandmother's sons
chunks.st: However, the certain sons of the elder woman, i.e., the mother-in-law,

chunks.en: may either do chalitzah or yibum,
chunks.st: perform either ḥalitza or levirate marriage,

chunks.en: because she is either his brother's wife
chunks.st: as with regard to each wife it is uncertain whether she is his brother’s wife, in which case levirate marriage is valid,

chunks.en: or his nephew's wife.
chunks.st: or his brother’s son’s wife, in which case she is permitted to him, after having performed ḥalitza with a son of the daughter-in-law.

chunks.en: If the sure sons died,
chunks.st: If the sons of certain, unflawed lineage were the ones who died, then

chunks.en: the mixed-up sons, with the grandmother's sons' widows,
chunks.st: the mixed sons perform

chunks.en: do chalitzah, but not yibum,
chunks.st: ḥalitza with the widows of the elder woman’s sons but not levirate marriage,

chunks.en: because she may be his brother's wife
chunks.st: as it is uncertain whether she is his brother’s wife

chunks.en: or his uncle's wife.
chunks.st: or his father’s brother’s wife.

chunks.en: And with the daughter-in-law's sons' widows,
chunks.st: With the widows of the certain sons of the daughter-in-law,

chunks.en: one does chalitzah and one does yibum.
chunks.st: one of the mixed sons performs ḥalitza, in case she is his brother’s wife. And the other one performs levirate marriage, as even if she is his brother’s son’s wife, she is permitted to him.

summary: A Kohen's wife's baby got mixed up with her maidservant's baby. Since each boy may be a Kohen or a slave, they get the strict rules of both, as the mishnah lists.

chunks.en: A Kohen's wife whose baby got mixed up with her maidservant's baby:
chunks.st: In the case of a priestess whose offspring was mixed with her maidservant’s offspring,

chunks.en: they may eat terumah,
chunks.explain: A Kohen's slave may also eat terumah.
chunks.st: they may partake of teruma, as both a priest and the slave of a priest partake of teruma.

chunks.en: and they get one share at the threshing floor.
chunks.st: And they receive one share of teruma in the granary.

chunks.en: They may not become tamei from the dead,
chunks.st: And they may not become ritually impure with impurity imparted by a corpse, as each of them might be a priest.

chunks.en: and they may not marry women,
chunks.st: And they may not marry women,

chunks.en: whether fit or unfit.
chunks.st: whether unflawed women, who may not marry a slave, or women unfit to marry into the priesthood, as with regard to each of them it is uncertain whether he is a priest or a slave.

chunks.en: If the mixed-up boys grew up
chunks.st: If the mixed sons matured

chunks.en: and freed each other,
chunks.st: and freed each other,

chunks.en: they may marry women fit for a Kohen.
chunks.st: they may marry women fit to marry into the priesthood, as a freed slave may marry such women. However, neither may marry a woman unfit for the priesthood, in case he is a priest.

chunks.en: They may not become tamei from the dead,
chunks.st: And they may not become ritually impure with impurity imparted by a corpse, since they are uncertain priests.

chunks.en: but if they did become tamei,
chunks.st: However, if they became impure,

chunks.en: they do not get the forty lashes.
chunks.st: they do not receive the forty lashes, as each of them might not be priest.

words.note: Forty lashes, a punishment of beis din.

chunks.en: They may not eat terumah,
chunks.st: And they may not partake of teruma, as one of them is not a priest.

chunks.en: but if they ate it,
chunks.st: However, if they ate teruma unwittingly

chunks.en: they do not pay back the amount plus a fifth.
chunks.st: they do not pay the principal and the additional fifth, as each of them might be a priest.

chunks.en: They do not get a share at the threshing floor.
chunks.st: And they do not receive a share of teruma in the granary, as neither can prove that he is a priest.

chunks.en: But they may sell their terumah,
chunks.st: However, they may sell the teruma that they remove from their own produce,

chunks.en: and the money is theirs.
chunks.st: and although they may not eat it, the money is theirs. Since it cannot be proven with regard to either of them that he is not a priest, teruma cannot be appropriated from them.

chunks.en: They do not get a share of the korbanos,
chunks.st: And they do not receive a share of the consecrated offerings of the Temple, as each of them might not be a priest.

chunks.en: and we do not give them korbanos to bring,
chunks.st: And one may not give them consecrated offerings to sacrifice for the same reason.

chunks.en: and we do not take their own away from them.
chunks.st: However, the hides of their own offerings may not be appropriated from their possession, as it cannot be proven with regard to either of them that he is not a priest.

chunks.en: They are free from giving the foreleg,
chunks.st: And they are exempt from giving a priest the foreleg, and from giving him

chunks.en: the jaw, and the stomach.
chunks.explain: Parts of an animal given to a Kohen.
chunks.st: the jaw, and from giving him the maw of their non-consecrated kosher animals.

chunks.en: And his bechor animal must graze until it gets a blemish,
chunks.st: And with regard to either of them, the firstling of his kosher animal should graze until it becomes unfit to be sacrificed, i.e., until it gets a blemish. It is against his interest to sacrifice the animal before it gets a blemish, thereby letting it be eaten by the priests. Once it gets a blemish, it cannot be appropriated from him. Since he is possibly a priest, he may claim that the animal is the property of a priest. The animal then becomes his private property, and he may eat it if he wishes. And in general,

chunks.he: וְנוֹתְנִין עָלָיו חֻמְרֵי כֹהֲנִים וְחֻמְרֵי יִשְׂרְאֵלִים:
chunks.en: and we give him the strict rules of Kohanim and of Yisraelim.
chunks.st: we place upon him both the stringencies of priests and the stringencies of Israelites.

summary: A woman remarried too soon and had a baby, and no one knows which husband is the father. The mishnah teaches what this son and his half-brothers do about yibum.

chunks.en: A woman who did not wait after
chunks.st: With regard to a woman who did not wait

chunks.en: her husband three months, and remarried,
chunks.st: three months after separating from her husband, and remarried

chunks.he: וְיָלְדָה, וְאֵין יָדוּעַ אִם בֶּן תִּשְׁעָה
chunks.en: and gave birth, and we do not know if he is a nine-month baby
chunks.st: and gave birth to a son, and it is not known if he was born after nine months of pregnancy

chunks.en: from the first, or a seven-month baby from the second.
chunks.st: to the former husband or if he was born after seven months to the latter husband, if

chunks.en: If she had sons from
chunks.st: she had sons of certain patrilineage

chunks.en: the first and sons from the second,
chunks.st: from the first husband and sons of certain patrilineage from the second one, and the son of uncertain patrilineage married and died childless, then the brothers from both husbands

chunks.en: they do chalitzah, but not yibum.
chunks.st: must perform ḥalitza with his wife, as they might be his paternal brothers. But they may not perform levirate marriage with her, in case he is only their maternal half brother, and his wife is forbidden to them.

chunks.en: And so he, for them,
chunks.st: And similarly, with regard to him and their wives, if one of them dies childless,

chunks.en: does chalitzah, but not yibum.
chunks.st: he performs ḥalitza and not levirate marriage. If

chunks.he: הָיוּ לוֹ אַחִים מִן הָרִאשׁוֹן וְאַחִים
chunks.en: If he had brothers from the first and brothers
chunks.st: he had half brothers from the first husband and half brothers

chunks.en: from the second, not from the same mother,
chunks.st: from the second, not from the same mother but from the same father,

chunks.en: he may do chalitzah or yibum,
chunks.st: he performs ḥalitza or levirate marriage with their widows.
chunks.stMore: If he is indeed their paternal half brother, then the widows are his yevamot; if not, he may marry them like any other man.

chunks.en: and for them, one does chalitzah and one does yibum.
chunks.st: And similarly, with regard to them and his wife, one half brother from one father performs ḥalitza and one from the other father performs levirate marriage.

summary: If the son's possible fathers were a Kohen and a regular Jew, he gets the strict rules of both. If both were Kohanim, he mourns for both and they for him, with other special rules.

chunks.en: If one was a regular Jew and one a Kohen,
chunks.st: If one of his two uncertain fathers was an Israelite and one was a priest,

chunks.en: he marries a woman fit for a Kohen,
chunks.st: he may marry only a woman fit to marry a priest, due to the possibility that he is a priest.

chunks.en: and he may not become tamei from the dead,
chunks.st: And he may not become ritually impure with impurity imparted by a corpse because he might be a priest.

chunks.en: but if he became tamei,
chunks.st: But if he became impure,

chunks.en: he does not get the forty lashes.
chunks.st: he does not receive the forty lashes, as he might be a non-priest.

chunks.en: He may not eat terumah,
chunks.st: Likewise, he does not partake of teruma, in case he is a non-priest.

chunks.en: but if he ate it,
chunks.st: However, if he ate teruma

chunks.en: he does not pay back the amount plus a fifth.
chunks.st: he does not pay the principal and the additional fifth, as he might be a priest.

chunks.en: He does not get a share at the threshing floor.
chunks.st: And he does not receive teruma at the granary.

chunks.en: But he may sell the terumah,
chunks.st: However, he may sell the teruma of his own produce

chunks.en: and the money is his.
chunks.st: and the money is his. It cannot be taken away from him due to the uncertainty with regard to his status.

chunks.en: He does not get a share of the korbanos,
chunks.st: And he does not receive a share of the sacred of the consecrated offerings,

chunks.en: and we do not give him korbanos to bring,
chunks.st: and one may not give him the consecrated offerings to sacrifice.

chunks.en: and we do not take his own away from him.
chunks.st: However, the hides of his own offerings may not be appropriated from his possession.

chunks.en: He is free from giving the foreleg, the jaw, and the stomach.
chunks.st: And he is exempt from giving a priest the foreleg, and the jaw, and the maw of his non-consecrated animals.

chunks.en: And his bechor animal must graze until it gets a blemish.
chunks.st: And the firstling of his animal should graze until it becomes unfit to be sacrificed because it gets a blemish.

chunks.he: וְנוֹתְנִין עָלָיו חֻמְרֵי כֹהֲנִים וְחֻמְרֵי יִשְׂרְאֵלִים.
chunks.en: And we give him the strict rules of Kohanim and of Yisraelim.
chunks.st: And in general, we place upon him the stringencies of priests and the stringencies of Israelites.

chunks.en: If both were Kohanim,
chunks.st: If both uncertain fathers were priests, then if they die

chunks.en: he mourns as an onein for them,
chunks.explain: An onein is a close mourner before the burial.
chunks.st: he is in a state of acute mourning over each of them, in case the deceased is his father.

chunks.en: and they mourn as onenim for him.
chunks.st: And if he dies, they are both in a state of acute mourning over him, as one of them is his father.

chunks.en: He may not become tamei for them,
chunks.st: He may not become ritually impure to bury them, as each one may not be his relative,

chunks.en: and they may not become tamei for him.
chunks.st: and they may not become ritually impure to bury him for the same reason.

chunks.en: He does not inherit from them,
chunks.st: He does not inherit from them, as the heirs of both husbands can reject his claims.

chunks.en: but they inherit from him.
chunks.st: However, they inherit from him if he has no sons and split his inheritance equally.

chunks.en: And he is not punished for hitting or cursing
chunks.st: And he is exempt from capital punishment for striking and for cursing

chunks.en: either one of them.
chunks.st: both this father and that one.
chunks.stMore: Although one who strikes or curses his father or mother is liable to receive the death penalty, he cannot be held liable, as it is unknown which of the men is his father.

chunks.he: וְעוֹלֶה בְמִשְׁמָרוֹ שֶׁל זֶה וְשֶׁל זֶה,
chunks.en: He goes up to serve with the mishmar of each one,
chunks.st: He must ascend to the Temple service with the priestly watch of this father and of that one, as he belongs to one of these watches and is obligated to serve with them.

words.note: The group of Kohanim who serve in the Mikdash that week.

chunks.en: but he does not get a share.
chunks.st: However, he does not receive a share of the portion of the offerings that gets eaten, as the members of each watch can claim that he is a member of the other watch.

chunks.en: If both were in one mishmar,
chunks.st: If both uncertain fathers were in one priestly watch,

chunks.en: he gets one share.
chunks.st: he receives one share, as he certainly belongs to that watch.
